subject: Intermittent API connection resets — egress path validation & next steps
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finservco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: API traffic — intermittent TLS resets and 504s after weekend maintenance

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures and 504 gateway responses to our Redwood-hosted inference endpoint after a maintenance window on our edge two nights ago. Impact: roughly 5-10% of requests from our batch workers are failing with connection reset/504s; latency spikes accompany it.

Attached is a short diagnostics dump from our edge (finserv_diag.txt). Key observations from our side:
- We see occasional ICMP "Fragmentation needed" messages in the flow snapshots.
- Traceroutes show an extra hop via our new palo-edge device added during maintenance.
- Problem seems worse for larger payloads (payload > 3KB).

This is urgent for us — can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's on-prem/private routing or NAT configuration on your side? We're happy to join a call.

Thanks,
Mike Turner
Platform Engineer, FinServCo
[Attachment: finserv_diag.txt]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finservco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API traffic — intermittent TLS resets and 504s after weekend maintenance

Hi Mike — thanks for the report and the attached diag. We're escalating this to our networking engineers. Quick notes and immediate asks to help narrow scope: 

1) Can you confirm whether the new palo-edge does MSS clamping / MTU changes? If so, what's the configured MTU and MSS clamp value?
2) Please run a short path-MTU test and a small/large curl compare to confirm size correlation (if you can provide traceroute -n and the path MTU output that helps).
3) We'll check NAT timeout metrics and symmetry on our egress layer (NAT gateways + dedicated on-prem edge).

Marcus and Dev — FYI I'm looping you both. Marcus: would you start by checking NAT session churn and security group logs for ephemeral port denials? Dev: please prepare an MSS workaround we can suggest to the customer if needed (iptables/snippet).

I'll keep this thread as the escalation channel.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-23T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API traffic — intermittent TLS resets and 504s after weekend maintenance

Kimberly / Mike — I pulled NAT metrics and packet drops from the egress cluster for the windows you reported. Preliminary findings: 

- NAT session churn is elevated on the affected nodes (session creation rate spikes around the same times FinServCo reported).
- We observed asymmetric return path for ~7% of sampled flows (ingress via node A, return via node B), likely because the new customer edge introduced a non-ideal AS path. Asymmetric flows are sensitive to stateful firewalls.
- tcpdump snippet attached (tcpdump-trim.pcap) shows a number of "RST"/"ICMP frag needed" for larger packets.
- Security group logs show occasional denies for ephemeral ports in the 49k-52k range between the egress NAT and the customer peer — looks like port mapping drift on the customer's NAT.

Next steps I'm recommending: 
- Run a path MTU probe from both sides to confirm where fragmentation is introduced.
- Short-term mitigation: enforce MSS clamping on the customer's palo-edge or apply MSS clamping at our edge on the NAT gateway for FinServCo's subnet.
- Medium-term: route affinity so flows from FinServCo maintain symmetric path through the same NAT node (canary rule).

[Attachment: tcpdump-trim.pcap (pcap)]

Marcus
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finservco.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API traffic — intermittent TLS resets and 504s after weekend maintenance

Hi Mike — quick pragmatic steps we can try immediately while we investigate: 

1) MSS clamp on customer's edge (recommended): set tcp MSS to 1360 for outbound TCP to Redwood endpoints. That addresses fragmentation at TLS-level for 1–3KB payloads.

Example iptables snippet (attached as mss-fix.sh):
- iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360

2) If MSS clamp can't be applied on your hardware, we can enable MSS clamp on our NAT gateway for traffic from your prefix as a temporary toggle.
3) Marcus is coordinating an affinity policy so return path stays on the same NAT node. That will reduce failures from asymmetric routing.

I'll be available for a live troubleshooting session; propose a 30-minute window tomorrow.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mss-fix.sh]

From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finservco.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API traffic — intermittent TLS resets and 504s after weekend maintenance

Thanks Dev — we applied the MSS clamp at the palo-edge to 1360 and ran a 24-hour test. The rate of incidents dropped from ~7% to ~2%, so that helped, but we still see sporadic resets during sustained large batch runs.

We also pulled a Palo Alto session report and attached it (paloalto-session-report.pdf). It shows occasional NAT translation session timeouts and a spike in ICMP frag needed messages correlated with the resets. We suspect two remaining factors: 
- Our edge occasionally rebalances sessions across devices (we'll look into sticky sessions), and
- Palo Alto's default TCP reassembly behavior differs slightly which could explain sporadic failures for certain packet sizes.

Given the business impact, we'd like to schedule a live troubleshooting call this week (we can do 10:00–11:00 PST any day). Also opening a support case with Palo Alto unless you recommend a different vendor route.

Mike Turner
Platform Engineer, FinServCo
[Attachment: paloalto-session-report.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finservco.com>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation summary & action plan — FinServCo egress instability

Team — summary and next steps from this thread. We're keeping the customer on this thread for transparency.

Summary:
- Issue: intermittent TLS resets / 504s for FinServCo when sending larger payloads after their recent edge change.
- Root causes found so far: MTU/MSS mismatch + asymmetric routing + NAT session timeout/port mapping drift.
- Mitigation applied: Customer enabled MSS clamp to 1360 (reduced errors from ~7% to ~2%).

Immediate action items (owners / ETA):
- Marcus: enable temporary per-prefix MSS clamp on our NAT gateway for FinServCo to fully contain the test (ETA: 2 hours).
- Dev: validate and QA the iptables snippet for our gateways and prepare a rollback plan (ETA: today EOD).
- Hannah: coordinate a sticky-session canary so FinServCo flows remain on a single NAT node (ETA: 48 hours).
- Kimberly (me): coordinate a joint triage call with FinServCo and Palo Alto if necessary; propose Zoom tomorrow 10:30 PST — will confirm.
- Marcus: open an internal ticket referencing JIRA-3421 for long-term routing affinity and follow-up diagnostics.

Customer ask: they requested a live troubleshooting call and want Palo Alto engaged if session timeouts persist. Mike — we'll set up the Zoom and invite Palo Alto support if you open a case.

SLA / credits: I'll coordinate with finance/ops if this qualifies for a credit; filing internal escalation now.

Please reply with any blockers.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
